items.title: A convex mixture of probability laws is a probability law
items.statement: Let $(X,\mathcal A)$ be a measurable space, let $P,Q$ be probability measures on it, and let $t\in[0,1]$. The set function $M_t(A)=(1-t)P(A)+tQ(A)$ is a probability measure.

items.title: A common data law forces a two-point tail-loss bound
items.statement: Let $(\mathcal Z,\mathcal G,R)$ be a probability space and let $\Theta$ be a measurable space ([[def-measurable-space]]) with $\theta_0,\theta_1\in\Theta$. Let $\hat\theta:\mathcal Z\to\Theta$ be measurable and let $\ell:\Theta\times\Theta\to[0,+\infty]$ have measurable sections $a\mapsto\ell(\theta_i,a)$. If $\max\{\ell(\theta_0,a),\ell(\theta_1,a)\}\ge\kappa\ell(\theta_0,\theta_1)$ for every $a\in\Theta$, where $\kappa>0$, then $\max_{i=0,1}R\{\ell(\theta_i,\hat\theta)\ge\kappa\ell(\theta_0,\theta_1)\}\ge1/2$.

items.title: Gross-error contamination path
items.statement: For probability measures $F,H$ on a common measurable space $(X,\mathcal A)$ ([[def-probability-measure]]) and $0\le\epsilon\le1$, the gross-error path is $F_{\epsilon,H}=(1-\epsilon)F+\epsilon H$, a probability measure by [[lem-convex-mixture-of-probability-laws]]. For any $x\in X$, its point-contamination direction at $x$ is the specialization $H=\delta_x$ ([[def-dirac-measure]], [[prop-dirac-measure-is-a-probability-measure]]). The path is used for a derivative at $\epsilon=0$; the definition alone gives no uniform-in-$H$ remainder.

items.title: Huber contamination model
items.statement:
Given a statistical experiment $\{P_\theta:\theta\in\Theta\}$ on $(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)$ ([[def-statistical-experiment]]) and any probability measure $Q$ on that space ([[def-probability-measure]]), Huber's one-observation contamination law is
$$
P_{\epsilon,\theta,Q}=(1-\epsilon)P_\theta+\epsilon Q,\qquad 0\le\epsilon\le1.
$$
The mixture is a probability measure by [[lem-convex-mixture-of-probability-laws]]. In the sample-size-$n$ model, observations are iid from this law ([[def-identically-distributed-and-iid-random-variables]]). A worst-case $Q$ may be chosen separately for each $\theta$. This is an iid sampling model, distinct from a fixed gross-error direction and from sample replacement.

items.title: Adversarial sample replacement
items.statement:
For a statistical experiment $\{P_\theta\}$ from [[def-statistical-experiment]], sample size $N\ge1$, and replacement fraction $0\le\eta\le1$, equip $\mathcal X^N$ with its finite product sigma-algebra ([[def-product-sigma-algebra-and-finite-product-sigma-algebras]]). A sample-replacement coupling is a pair of $\mathcal X^N$-valued random elements on a common probability space ([[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]]) $(X,Y)$ such that $X_1,\ldots,X_N$ are iid with law $P_\theta$ under [[def-identically-distributed-and-iid-random-variables]] and
$$
\sum_{i=1}^N\mathbf1\{X_i\ne Y_i\}\le\lfloor\eta N\rfloor
$$
almost surely. Assume the diagonal $\Delta_{\mathcal X}=\{(x,x):x\in\mathcal X\}$ belongs to the product sigma-algebra $\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A$ ([[def-product-sigma-algebra-and-finite-product-sigma-algebras]]), so each mismatch indicator is measurable. The joint law may depend on the entire clean sample; the observed vector $Y$ need not be iid.

items.title: TV-close laws have identical Huber mixtures at the contamination threshold
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $P_0,P_1$ be probability measures on one measurable space. If $0\le\epsilon<1$ and $\|P_0-P_1\|_{TV}\le\epsilon/(1-\epsilon)$, there are probability measures $Q_0,Q_1$ for which
$$
(1-\epsilon)P_0+\epsilon Q_0=(1-\epsilon)P_1+\epsilon Q_1.
$$
At $\epsilon=1$, the same equality is possible without a TV condition.

items.title: Contamination-robust expected risk and tail risk
items.statement:
Let the experiment in [[def-statistical-experiment]] have nonempty parameter set $\Theta$. Choose a sigma-algebra $\mathcal T$ on $\Theta$ and take $(\Theta,\mathcal T)$ as its measurable action space ([[def-measurable-space]]). Specialize the target-first loss of [[def-loss-function-and-risk]] to $L:\Theta\times\Theta\to[0,+\infty]$ by taking its action space to be $(\Theta,\mathcal T)$. Fix an integer sample size $N\ge1$ and a measurable rule $\hat\theta:\mathcal X^N\to\Theta$. Equip $\mathcal X^N$ with the finite product sigma-algebra ([[def-product-sigma-algebra-and-finite-product-sigma-algebras]]); the iid sample law is the finite product measure supplied by [[def-product-measure-on-sigma-finite-spaces]] and [[thm-sigma-finite-product-measure-exists-is-rectangular-and-is-unique]]. Write $X(x)=x$ for the canonical sample vector on this product space. The Huber sampling law is from [[def-huber-contamination-model]], and nonnegative expectations use [[def-expectation-of-a-nonnegative-or-integrable-random-variable]]. For $0\le\epsilon\le1$ and $0\le\eta\le1$, its **Huber robust expected risk** at fraction $\epsilon$ is
$$
\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\sup_Q\mathbb E_{P_{\epsilon,\theta,Q}^{\otimes N}}L(\theta,\hat\theta(X)).
$$
Its **replacement robust expected risk** at fraction $\eta$ is the supremum of $\mathbb E L(\theta,\hat\theta(Y))$ over $\theta$ and all couplings in [[def-adversarial-sample-replacement]]. For $t\in[0,+\infty]$, the Huber tail risk at threshold $t$ is $\sup_{\theta,Q}P_{\epsilon,\theta,Q}^{\otimes N}\{x:L(\theta,\hat\theta(x))\ge t\}$; the replacement tail risk is the supremum of $\Pr\{L(\theta,\hat\theta(Y))\ge t\}$ over $\theta$ and the same replacement couplings. Expected risk and tail risk are different criteria. The gross-error path in [[def-gross-error-path]] is a path of laws; it is not a sample-replacement mechanism.

items.title: Huber contamination modulus
items.statement:
For an experiment $\{P_\theta:\theta\in\Theta\}$ with nonempty $\Theta$ ([[def-statistical-experiment]]), choose a sigma-algebra $\mathcal T$ on $\Theta$ and take $(\Theta,\mathcal T)$ as the measurable action space ([[def-measurable-space]]). Take the target-first loss $L:\Theta\times\Theta\to[0,+\infty]$ from [[def-loss-function-and-risk]] with that action space. For $0\le\epsilon<1$, define
$$
\omega(\epsilon,\Theta)=\sup\{L(\theta_1,\theta_2):\theta_1,\theta_2\in\Theta,\ \|P_{\theta_1}-P_{\theta_2}\|_{TV}\le\epsilon/(1-\epsilon)\}.
$$
Set $\omega(1,\Theta)=\sup_{\theta_1,\theta_2\in\Theta}L(\theta_1,\theta_2)$, allowing $+\infty$. Total variation is the event-supremum convention $\sup_A|P(A)-Q(A)|$ from [[def-total-variation-distance-for-probability-laws]], with no factor $1/2$.

items.title: Huber contamination modulus lower bound for tail risk
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix a contamination level $0\le\epsilon\le1$, an integer sample size $N\ge1$, and a nonempty statistical model $\{P_\theta:\theta\in\Theta\}$ on a common measurable sample space, and give $\Theta$ a measurable structure as the parameter action space ([[def-measurable-space]]). Let the target-first loss $L:\Theta\times\Theta\to[0,+\infty]$ of [[def-loss-function-and-risk]] have measurable sections $a\mapsto L(\theta,a)$. Suppose a fixed $0<\kappa\le1$ satisfies
$$
\max\{L(\theta_0,a),L(\theta_1,a)\}\ge\kappa L(\theta_0,\theta_1)
$$
for all $a,\theta_0,\theta_1\in\Theta$. Suppose also that $0\le M_0<\infty$, $0<c_0\le1$, and
$$
\inf_{\hat\theta:\mathcal X^N\to\Theta\ {\rm measurable}}\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}P_{\theta}^{\otimes N}\{L(\theta,\hat\theta)\ge M_0\}\ge c_0.
$$
If $\omega(\epsilon,\Theta)<\infty$, then with
$$
M_\epsilon=\frac{\kappa}{4}\bigl(M_0\vee\omega(\epsilon,\Theta)\bigr)
$$
one has
$$
\inf_{\hat\theta:\mathcal X^N\to\Theta\ {\rm measurable}}\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\sup_QP_{\epsilon,\theta,Q}^{\otimes N}\{L(\theta,\hat\theta)\ge M_\epsilon\}\ge\min(c_0,1/2).
$$
Thus the lower-bound threshold is comparable to $M_0\vee\omega(\epsilon,\Theta)$. If $\omega(\epsilon,\Theta)=+\infty$, the same supremum is at least $1/2$ at every finite threshold. In particular, if $c_0\ge c_*>0$ for a fixed constant $c_*\le1/2$ independent of the model, the finite-modulus conclusion has the universal probability constant $c_*$. A metric loss has the separation property with $\kappa=1/2$; its square has it with $\kappa=1/4$.

items.title: The mean has an unbounded directional derivative supremum
items.statement: On $\mathbb R$ with its Borel sigma-algebra, for $F=\delta_0$ and $H=\delta_a$, the mean functional $T(G)=\int x\,dG(x)$ has $T(F_{\epsilon,H})=\epsilon a$ and right derivative $a$ at $\epsilon=0$. Each path law has finite support and hence a finite first moment. Taking the supremum of the absolute derivatives over $a\in\mathbb R$ gives $+\infty$.

items.title: Bounded sample-mean change under replacements and a common corrupted sample
items.statement:
For integers $N\ge1$ and $0\le k\le N$, if $x_i,y_i\in[0,1]$ and at most $k$ coordinates differ, then
$$
\left|N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N y_i-N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N x_i\right|\le k/N.
$$
For the coupling example, take $\mathcal X=\Theta=\{0,1\}$ with their full power-set sigma-algebras ([[def-measurable-space]]) and the experiment $P_\theta=\delta_\theta$ ([[def-statistical-experiment]], [[def-dirac-measure]], [[prop-dirac-measure-is-a-probability-measure]]). For $N=2$ and replacement fraction $\eta=1/2$, the clean samples $(0,0)$ and $(1,1)$ can both be changed to $(0,1)$ with one replacement, so the two parameter values induce the same observed law.

items.title: Exact Bernoulli Huber modulus and indistinguishable mixtures
items.statement:
Take $\Theta=[0,1]$ with its Borel sigma-algebra and sample space $\{0,1\}$ with full power set. Let $\delta_0,\delta_1$ be the point masses, set $P_\theta=(1-\theta)\delta_0+\theta\delta_1$, and use absolute parameter loss $L(\theta,a)=|\theta-a|$. Then
$$
\omega(\epsilon,\Theta)=\min\{\epsilon/(1-\epsilon),1\}\quad(0\le\epsilon<1),\qquad \omega(1,\Theta)=1.
$$
For $0<\epsilon\le1/2$, set $\theta_0=0$, $\theta_1=\epsilon/(1-\epsilon)$, $Q_0=\delta_1$, and $Q_1=\delta_0$; both Huber mixtures are Bernoulli$(\epsilon)$. For $1/2\le\epsilon\le1$, endpoint laws can also be made identical.
